title: Localization of a morphism of ringed sites
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites and let $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ be a continuous functor defining a morphism of sites $f:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, so that $f_*G(T)=G(u(T))$ and its left adjoint $f^{-1}$ preserves finite limits [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $R$ on $\mathcal D$ and $S$ on $\mathcal C$ be sheaves of commutative rings, with a ring map $c:f^{-1}R\to S$. For $V\in\mathcal D$ put $U=u(V)$ and give $\mathcal D/V$ and $\mathcal C/U$ the localized topology and restricted coefficient sheaves [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. The functor $u_V:(T\to V)\mapsto(u(T)\to u(V))$ defines a morphism of sites $f_V:\mathcal C/U\to\mathcal D/V$. There is a canonical natural isomorphism $(f_V)^{-1}j_V^{-1}\cong j_U^{-1}f^{-1}$, making the localization square commute as morphisms of topoi. The ring map for $f_V$ is $(f_V)^{-1}(R|_V)\cong(f^{-1}R)|_U\xrightarrow{c|_U}S|_U$. Use sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For the module pullbacks $f^*M=S\otimes_{f^{-1}R}f^{-1}M$ and $(f_V)^*H=(S|_U)\otimes_{(f_V)^{-1}(R|_V)}(f_V)^{-1}H$, and module direct images with ring action through the adjuncts of these ring maps [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction], the square commutes as morphisms of ringed topoi, and there are canonical natural isomorphisms
$$ (f_V)^*j_V^*\cong j_U^*f^*,\qquad j_V^*f_*\cong(f_V)_*j_U^*. $$
The direct-image comparison on an object $T\to V$ is the identity $G(u(T))=G|_U(u(T)\to U)$ with its restricted $R(T)$-action.

source.place: Tag 04J0, lemma-localize-morphism-ringed-sites; underlying slice-site construction: sites.tex Tag 03CF, lemma-localize-morphism

proof.text: Apply the underlying slice-site localization lemma (Stacks Tag 03CF) to u and V. It gives the continuous functor u_V, the induced morphism f_V, the canonical isomorphism (f_V)^{-1}j_V^{-1}≅j_U^{-1}f^{-1}, and the direct-image identity j_V^{-1}f_*≅(f_V)_*j_U^{-1}.
Define the localized ring map by (f_V)^{-1}(R|_V)≅(f^{-1}R)|_U→S|_U, using the inverse-image isomorphism from Step 1 and the restriction of c. The ring-map square therefore commutes by construction.

First $j^*=j^{-1}$ for a localization: its ring map is the identity on the restricted ring, so the tensor formula in the module-adjunction node reduces to $\mathcal O_U\otimes_{\mathcal O_U}M|_U\cong M|_U$, by $a\otimes m\mapsto am$ with inverse $m\mapsto1\otimes m$. Taking right adjoints of the inverse-image square of Step 1 gives $j_{V*}(f_V)_*\cong f_*j_{U*}$: for any sheaves $A,H$, both Hom sets are identified by adjunction with $\operatorname{Hom}((f_V)^{-1}j_V^{-1}A,H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(j_U^{-1}f^{-1}A,H)$. This is also an isomorphism of module functors. Indeed the coefficient map $R\to j_{V*}(f_V)_*(S|_U)$ is adjunct to the composite $(f_V)^{-1}j_V^{-1}R\to S|_U$ of Step 2; the map $R\to f_*j_{U*}(S|_U)$ is adjunct to $j_U^{-1}f^{-1}R\xrightarrow{c|_U}S|_U$. Step 2 identifies these maps, so the right-adjoint isomorphism respects the $R$-actions. Now apply the cited module adjunction twice on each side: for every $R$-module $M$ and $S|_U$-module $H$,
$$ \operatorname{Hom}((f_V)^*j_V^*M,H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,j_{V*}(f_V)_*H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,f_*j_{U*}H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(j_U^*f^*M,H). $$
These natural bijections give the desired canonical pullback isomorphism (apply them to the identity maps to obtain the two inverse arrows). Finally, on $T\to V$ both $j_V^*f_*G$ and $(f_V)_*j_U^*G$ are $G(u(T))$. If $a:R\to f_*S$ is adjunct to $c$, the scalar $r\in R(T)$ acts on both by multiplication by $a_T(r)\in S(u(T))$; the localized adjunct has component $a_T$ by Step 2. Thus the sectionwise identity is linear, commutes with restriction maps and with morphisms in $G$, and yields the asserted natural module direct-image isomorphism.
